title: Energy, Work & the Role of ATP
description: Why cells need a rechargeable energy currency, and how ATP stores and releases energy through its phosphate bonds.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain why ATP is called the energy currency of the cell and describe what happens when ATP is hydrolysed to ADP.

title: Redox Reactions & Electron Carriers
description: Oxidation and reduction as electron transfer, and how NAD+ and FAD shuttle electrons during respiration.
mastery_criteria: Student can identify which species is oxidised and which is reduced in a reaction and explain the role of NAD+/NADH.

title: Reading a Metabolic Pathway Diagram
description: How to interpret the arrows, enzymes and intermediates in a metabolic pathway map.
mastery_criteria: Student can trace substrates to products through a pathway diagram and name the enzyme catalysing a given step.

title: Glucose as a Fuel Molecule
description: The structure of glucose and why its bonds hold the chemical energy respiration extracts.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain where the energy in glucose is stored and why it must be released stepwise.

title: Glycolysis: The Ten-Step Overview
description: The overall input and output of glycolysis and its split into energy-investment and energy-payoff phases.
mastery_criteria: Student can state the net ATP, NADH and pyruvate yield of glycolysis from one glucose.

title: Regulating Glycolysis
description: How phosphofructokinase and feedback inhibition tune the rate of glycolysis to the cell's energy needs.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain how ATP and AMP levels regulate phosphofructokinase activity.

title: Pyruvate Oxidation & Acetyl-CoA
description: How pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA, linking glycolysis to the citric acid cycle.
mastery_criteria: Student can describe the decarboxylation of pyruvate and the formation of acetyl-CoA and NADH.

title: The Citric Acid Cycle
description: The eight-step cycle that fully oxidises acetyl-CoA, producing NADH, FADH2 and GTP.
mastery_criteria: Student can state the per-cycle yield of NADH, FADH2 and ATP/GTP and where CO2 is released.

title: Regulation of the Citric Acid Cycle
description: How NADH and ATP concentrations feed back to control the pace of the cycle.
mastery_criteria: Student can name the regulated enzymes of the cycle and explain how energy charge controls them.

title: Mitochondrial Membrane Architecture
description: The inner and outer membranes, cristae and matrix, and why compartmentation matters for respiration.
mastery_criteria: Student can label the mitochondrial compartments and explain the role of the inner membrane.

title: The Electron Transport Chain
description: How complexes I-IV pass electrons down an energy gradient and pump protons across the inner membrane.
mastery_criteria: Student can order the electron carriers by redox potential and explain proton pumping.

title: The Proton Gradient & Chemiosmosis
description: How the proton-motive force stores energy across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
mastery_criteria: Student can define the proton-motive force and explain how it couples the ETC to ATP synthesis.

title: ATP Synthase Mechanism
description: Plain-language explanation of how ATP synthase converts a proton gradient into chemical energy.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain the three stages of chemiosmosis and name the enzyme involved.

title: Accounting for the Total ATP Yield
description: Adding up ATP from glycolysis, the cycle and oxidative phosphorylation per glucose.
mastery_criteria: Student can calculate the approximate total ATP yield from one glucose and justify each contribution.

title: Anaerobic Respiration & Fermentation
description: What happens when oxygen is absent, and how fermentation regenerates NAD+ to keep glycolysis running.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain why fermentation is needed anaerobically and compare its yield to aerobic respiration.

title: Integrating Respiration with Whole-Cell Metabolism
description: How respiration connects to fat and protein catabolism and adjusts to the cell's changing demands.
mastery_criteria: Student can describe how fats and amino acids feed into respiration and how the whole system is regulated.
